findings.title: [P1] Return the declared `id` field instead of `userId` in `loadUser`
findings.body: `loadUser` is declared as `Promise<User>` with `User = { id: string; name: string }` (unchanged by this PR), but the rewritten return produces `{ userId: row.id, name: row.display_name }`. Required property `id` is missing and `userId` is not declared on `User`, so this object literal fails type checking against the declared return type; if type checking is bypassed (plain JS), any consumer reading `result.id` now gets `undefined`. This directly contradicts the PR's stated goal of preserving existing contracts. Either restore `id: row.id` in the returned object, or — if `userId` is the intended new shape — update the `User` type and every consumer of it in the same change. No in-repo callers of `loadUser` exist to catch this today, which is exactly why the type contract must stay authoritative.
